newsitem.title: USA: New York Bagel sees higher Q4 net, sales.
newsitem.headline: New York Bagel sees higher Q4 net, sales.

text.p: New York Bagel Enterprises Inc said Monday it expects to report earnings of between $0.04 and $0.05 a share for the fourth quarter, up from year-ago pro forma earnings of $0.02 a share.
Total revenues for the quarter rose to $3.3 million from $2.0 million a year ago.
The company said these preliminary results do not include any possible fourth-quarter adjustments.

New York Bagel said the rise in its revenues was tempered by higher percentage labor costs and higher depreciation and amortization expenses, primarily due to new restaurant openings and the acquisition of Lots A' Bagels.
Final results for the fourth quarter are expected to be reported on or about February 6.

New York Bagel said its same-restaurant sales in the fourth quarter rose 4.6 percent. In addition, sales from company-owned restaurants increased to $3.3 million from $1.9 million in the year-ago quarter. As of December 29, New York Bagel had 33 company-owned restaurants, up from 15 a year ago.
New York Bagel completed its acquisition of Lots A' Bagels in December in a deal valued at $2.7 million.

"Our strategic growth remains on track," Paul Hoover, vice president - strategic planning, added. "We expect the Lots 'A Bagels acquisition...to significantly contribute to 1997 results. We will continue to develop company-owned restaurants and make strategic acquisitions."

For the fiscal year, based upon fourth quarter earnings estimates, the company expects to report full-year earnings of about $0.18 a share, compared with pro forma net earnings of $0.13 for 1995. Total revenues were $11.4 million for the year, up 54.8 percent from $7.4 million in 1995.
Same-restaurant sales for the year were up 4.4 percent.
New York Bagel completed an initial public offering in August 1996.
